result:
The condition d < M/100 is equivalent to M/d > 100. So M is imbalanced exactly when the number t of divisors of M that are ≤ 100 satisfies t < 0.01·τ(M), that is, τ(M) > 100t.

Since 2000 | M, every divisor of 2000 is a divisor of M. The divisors of 2000 that are ≤ 100 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 16, 20, 25, 40, 50, 80, 100, which is 13 divisors. So t ≥ 13 and τ(M) > 1300. Solution 2 lists 100 but counts only 12, so its bound is wrong, and Solution 1 also uses 12.

To have t = 13 exactly:
- The exponent of 2 must be 4, because 32 would otherwise be an extra divisor ≤ 100.
- The exponent b of 5 can be any value ≥ 3, since 5⁴ = 625 > 100 adds no new small divisors.
- Any other prime factor must exceed 100.

Then τ(M) = 5(b+1)·K for some integer K, so τ(M) is a multiple of 5. The smallest multiple of 5 above 1300 is 1305 = 5·261. It is achieved by M = 2⁴·5²⁶⁰, which has t = 13 and τ(M) = 1305 > 1300.

A larger t only raises the bound τ(M) > 100t, so the minimum is 1305.

Solution 1 gives 1320 and Solution 2 gives 1220, both from miscounting t as 12. Solution 3 gives 1305, which is correct.
